_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: The Edge Theatre & Arts Centre
suggestions.reason: A former Red Cross hospital on Manchester Road doing double duty as Chorlton's own theatre, gallery and community cinema — the programme changes hands often enough that a second visit rarely repeats the first.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via edgetheatre.co.uk, futureartscentres.org.uk, chorlton.coop and whatsonstage.com — a real, currently operating independent theatre and arts charity (not a chain; single site, run as a charity working with homeless people, vulnerable adults and young people alongside its public programme) at Manchester Road, Chorlton, M21 9JG. No closure signals found; multiple current event/venue listings. Coordinates are the M21 9JG postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk), not invented. Type mapped to existing PERFORMING ARTS (Do), same precedent as Green Room Theatre/Chads Theatre for a community-run amateur/charity venue. High confidence.

suggestions.name: The Chorlton Tap
suggestions.reason: Wilbraham Road's real-ale room since the late nineties, back when it was just called The Bar — fourteen keg lines, four cask, and a wood-fired oven doing pizza out front on the nights it fancies it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk/pubs/chorlton-tap-chorlton-cum-hardy-130156), whatpub.com, Untappd and Instagram (@thechorltontap) — a real, currently trading, single-site independent real-ale pub at 533 Wilbraham Road, M21 0UE (formerly 'The Bar', one of Chorlton's first modern cafe-bars in the late 90s). No sister-site or chain footprint found under this name; it stocks (but does not appear to be owned by) Wander Beyond Brewing, whose own taproom is a separate site under Piccadilly station — flagged for the reviewer to double-check ownership structure at promotion time. No closure signals. Coordinates are the M21 0UE postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing ALE HOUSE (Drink, category-only, previously only used for the now-removed Old Dancer) — a real-ale-first pub matches this type better than COUNTRY PUB or WINE BAR. Moderate-high confidence.

suggestions.name: Bar San Juan
suggestions.reason: Fifteen years on Beech Road and counting — proper Spanish tapas, sherry by the glass, and a Neighbourhood Venue of the Year plaque behind the bar the locals would tell you is deserved.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via barsanjuan.com, Tripadvisor, OpenTable and manchestersfinest.com — a real, currently operating, single-site independent tapas restaurant at 56 Beech Road, Chorlton, M21 9EG, trading since 2010, named in the Good Food Guide 2025 and Manchester Food & Drink Festival's Neighbourhood Venue of the Year. No chain footprint or closure signals found. Coordinates are the M21 9EG postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing SMALL PLATES (Eat) — tapas is a direct fit. High confidence. Note for the reviewer: The Jane Eyre (already seeded in Ancoats) also opened a genuine second site on Beech Road, Chorlton in Dec 2025 — a real, verifiable sibling-site expansion — but deliberately not suggested here to avoid a same-name collision with the existing Ancoats entry; worth a considered decision (rename/disambiguate?) rather than a silent skip if Chorlton's Eat coverage still needs more later.

suggestions.name: White Peak Alpaca Farm
suggestions.reason: Jake and Joanna's own herd on Paddock Hill, pre-booked walks only — the sort of unhurried Cheshire afternoon that doesn't need a restaurant attached to justify the drive out.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via whitepeakalpacafarm.co.uk, Tripadvisor (including a February 2026-dated review confirming current operation) and eastcheshire.mumbler.co.uk — a real, currently operating, family-run (Jake and Joanna), single-site alpaca farm experience at Paddock Hill, Mobberley, Knutsford WA16 7DB. No chain footprint (a working smallholding) and no closure signals. Coordinates are the WA16 7DB postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Introduces a new type, FARM EXPERIENCE (Do) — no existing type fits a pre-booked animal-encounter attraction; FARM SHOP already exists but is mapped Eat-only and describes a different kind of venue (Waugh Brow's counter-and-café). Fills a real gap: Mobberley's Do category was tied for thinnest at 2 venues alongside Drink. High confidence on operating status; flagged for the reviewer to add the new type to tile-catalog-map.ts's CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE on promotion.

suggestions.name: Inch Arts
suggestions.reason: The old town library's ground floor, now a working charity of studios, a makerspace and a gallery that changes hands as often as the artists teaching in it — free to walk into, on Stamford New Road.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via inch-arts.co.uk, creativetourist.com and the Charity Commission register (a registered CIO since 2018) — a real, currently operating, single-site independent arts charity and gallery at 20 Stamford New Road, Altrincham WA14 1EJ, occupying the ground floor of the old town library. No closure signals found (active Eventbrite/Instagram/Facebook listings; no explicit current-year confirmation found, but no evidence of closure or relocation either after a direct check). Coordinates are the WA14 1EJ postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing ART GALLERY (Do), same precedent as The Horsfall/esea contemporary for a charity-run gallery/studio space. Fills a real gap: Altrincham's Do category is thinnest at 2 venues (Everyman Cinema, Altrincham Market). Moderate-high confidence.

suggestions.name: The Blind Pig
suggestions.reason: A courtyard door off King Street with no sign worth mentioning, four keg lines and a cocktail list that never quite repeats itself — Porto next door if the wait's too long.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via theblindpig.uk, camra.org.uk/pubs/blind-pig-knutsford-198873, discoverknutsford.com and Instagram (@theblindpigknutsford) — a real, currently operating speakeasy-style cocktail bar at 1 Red Cow Yard, Knutsford WA16 6DG. Shares ownership with Porto, a second bar in the same courtyard — a same-town, two-site sibling pair, the same precedent as Cibo/Suburban Green/Wallop elsewhere in this dataset, not a wider chain footprint. No closure signals. Coordinates approximated from neighbouring WA16 6 postcodes in the same King Street/Red Cow Yard cluster (doogal.co.uk did not resolve this exact postcode directly) — street-level, not a district centroid. Type mapped to existing SPEAKEASY (Drink), same as Blinker (Northern Quarter). Fills a real gap: Knutsford's Drink category is tied for thinnest at 2 venues. Moderate-high confidence — coordinate precision slightly below this file's usual bar since the exact postcode didn't resolve directly; flagged for the reviewer to double-check.

suggestions.name: Les Deux Pizza Bar
suggestions.reason: The little pink door on London Road hides a forty-eight-hour dough and a cocktail list built to match it — dog-friendly, hoodie-friendly, and unbothered by the dress code further up the strip.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, ilovemanchester.com, vivamanchester.co.uk and alderleyedge.com — a real, currently operating, single-site independent pizza-and-cocktail bar at 7 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7JT, opened by Mathieu Everson and Sax (the latter also linked to Mughli, Evelyn's Cafe Bar and The Daisy — distinctly named, distinctly conceived venues under one operator across Manchester/Cheshire, not a replicated chain brand; no second site trading under the Les Deux name itself was found). No closure signals. Coordinates are the SK9 7JT postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing PIZZERIA (Eat), same as La Cucina/Rudy's — distinct in register (cocktail-forward, dog-friendly) despite the shared type. Fills a real gap: Alderley Edge is one of the furthest-under-10 districts at 6 real venues. Moderate-high confidence.

suggestions.name: InHale Yoga
suggestions.reason: A first-floor studio on Cecil Road running vinyasa before work and ashtanga after it — small classes, real teachers' names on the timetable, not a franchise's booking app.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via inhaleyoga.co.uk (a current, live 2026-dated class timetable), Facebook (@yogainhale) and Happity — a real, currently operating, single-site independent yoga and pilates studio at First Floor, Progress House, 17 Cecil Road, Hale, Altrincham WA15 9NZ. No chain footprint or closure signals. Coordinates are the nearest resolvable postcode on the same Cecil Road (WA15 9NX, doogal.co.uk) — the exact WA15 9NZ postcode didn't resolve directly, so this is street-level rather than building-level, consistent with this file's usual precision. Type mapped to existing WELLNESS STUDIO (Do), same as Wilmslow Pilates & Wellness. Fills a real gap: Hale's Do category is thinnest at 2 venues. High confidence on operating status (live current timetable), moderate on exact coordinate precision.

suggestions.name: Lions Den
suggestions.reason: Two hundred capacity on Deansgate Mews, built and still run by one promoter twenty years into the job — open mic on a Wednesday, a proper touring act by the weekend.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thegreatnorthern.com (the venue's own listing within the Great Northern complex), gigseekr.com (current event listings), skiddle.com and manchestersfinest.com — a real, currently operating, single-site independent live music venue and bar at Deansgate Mews, 235 Deansgate, M3 4EN, owned and run by promoter Dave Foran. No chain footprint (a tenant within the Great Northern building, not part of a multi-site bar group) and no closure signals. Coordinates are the M3 4EN postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing LIVE MUSIC (Do), same as Band on the Wall/Hallé St Peter's. Fills a real gap: Deansgate's Do category is thinnest at 2 venues. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Australasia
suggestions.reason: A glass pyramid entrance on The Avenue and a Pacific Rim share-plates menu re-set under new ownership this year — sushi and southeast Asian flavours in the basement room that started Spinningfields' whole restaurant scene back in 2011.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, ilovemanchester.com and australasiamcr.co.uk — a real, currently operating restaurant at 1 The Avenue, Spinningfields, M3 3AP, open since 2011 and recently relaunched under new operator Orka Koncepts (acquired from Living Ventures). Orka Koncepts also runs Grand Pacific and Dear Sailor (both Manchester city centre) plus a catering business — a small, same-city multi-venue operator, not a multi-city chain, the same precedent as Higher Ground/Flawd/Bar Shrimp's shared ownership elsewhere in this dataset. No closure signals — recent relaunch coverage confirms it's trading. Coordinates are the M3 3AP postcode centroid (doogal.co.uk). Type mapped to existing SMALL PLATES (Eat) over FINE DINING, matching its share-plates format. Fills a real gap: Spinningfields' Eat category is thinnest at 2 venues (Ivy, Tattu). High confidence.
